Outstanding resource. Copy-paste could use a tweak.. Outstanding resource. Use it almost every day. The fineness of its translation (I have worked extensively with Greek and can confirm, an MDiv and a ThM in exegetical theology). The search function is outstanding and simple. I use it often when knowing a verse but struggling to remember where it is found. Also just the look throughout is subtle and elegant to my eyes. It is crisp, easy and user-friendly. 

I would personally reformat a couple very minor things for a regular user, like the copy-paste function which puts the verse reference first and even the non-inspired section title into the paste (why?) before pasting the words. It’d be much easier to simply paste the verse words, with reference on its tail, like this: “Jesus wept” (John 11:35). The current way makes it hard to copy-paste into texts for encouragement and social media. Every single time I copy-paste I have to edit it. 

Aside from that, an outstanding resource. I use it almost every single day. “Forever, o Lord, your word is firmly fixed in the heavens.” Psalm 119:89.

reviews.text:
The Bible App That Quietly Outsmarts Every Other One. There are a lot of Bible apps that try to do everything. This one chose to do the right things exceptionally well.

The ESV Bible App from Crossway feels less like software and more like a well-crafted tool refined, intentional, and built to get out of the way so you can actually engage with Scripture.

The first thing that stands out is the balance of form and function this feels like it was forged in heaven, as if built by the hands of Dieter Rams himself. Here are just a few of the heavenly hallmarks: The UI and UX are remarkably clean, but not at the expense of power. You can jump to any chapter and verse in seconds, or search a fragment of a verse and find exactly what you’re looking for just as fast. No detours, no “let me Google this real quick.” It respects your time and your focus.

Then there’s the ecosystem. Whether you’re on iPhone, iPad, or desktop, everything just syncs. Seamlessly. Notes, highlights, position it all carries over without friction. It feels like it belongs in the Apple world: quiet, reliable, and invisible when it should be. Of note, I like the browser version on Mac desktop - the desktop app has some limitations with its ability to highlight several verses at the same time, while the browser does not.

Design-wise, this app shows rare restraint. You’re not buried under endless customization options. You get a thoughtful set of fonts, a few highlighter colors, and that’s it. And that’s exactly right. It’s disciplined. Focused. Keeps you on the subject matter, not distractions. More like a finely tuned instrument than a control panel with a hundred switches.

The audio feature is another standout. With the paid version, you get a range of voices and adjustable playback speeds, turning reading into something you can carry with you on a walk, in the car, wherever. It’s not a gimmick, it’s genuinely useful.

What really sets this app apart, though, is what it doesn’t do. No clutter. No distractions. No competing noise. Just Scripture, your notes, and thoughtful cross-references. It keeps the main thing the main thing.

In a world full of apps trying to add more, this one succeeds by knowing what to leave out.

And that makes all the difference.

reviews.text:
RECENT UPDATE: BUGS, A DOWNGRADE, AND LAYOUT. I’ve been using the app for years and this hands down has to be the worst update. It functions not like an app that’s been well refined but more akin to a first generation app with many navigation bugs along with a downgrade in functionality. (For what it’s worth, I’m using an iPhone 12 fully updated.) 

 NAVIGATION BUGS 1. Whenever I close the app and then return, it goes to Genesis 1, not to where I last finished reading. 2. When I tap on any of the four daily readings inside my (M'Cheyne) reading plan, it takes me to the first reading. For example, today’s readings included Exodus, Luke, Job, and 1 Corinthians. Tap on any of them and it takes me to the Exodus reading. 3. When I tap on the book at the top of the screen, I get the drop down menu of the books of the Bible. Regardless of which one I tap on, it takes me to Genesis 1. 4. Today I was using the audio in the Proverbs reading plan. As I was manually scrolling between chapters 3 and 4, it instead jumped to reading Proverbs 5. 6. The timer that sets a pause between chapters does not function inside a reading plan. 

DOWNGRADE I don’t know why the audio speed control would have been downgraded to presets only: .75, 1.00, etc. In the previous version, the user could “fine tune” the playback speed. I know this is a matter of personal preference, but there are certain literary genres, for instance poetry and wisdom, that need to be slowed down to less than .75. And adding a .5 preset won’t address this problem. I’ve tried this speed in another app and it’s way to slow. But my point is this: Regardless of personal preferences, why downgrade this functionality? This was not an improvement.

LAYOUT Anytime an app is changed, it takes time to get accustomed to the new layout. But like other reviewers have already described in greater detail, and I agree, the previous version was way better. It, in fact, needed no “update”. I contacted Crossway to see if I could revert to the previous version. Unfortunately, that was not an option. 

 In spite of my “negative” review, I appreciate Crossway making this app available. I have enjoyed and greatly benefited from it for years. Thank you, Crossway.

reviews.text:
Recent update has damaged the app’s decency. I review this app as someone who has used this app for years (as long as I can remember). This most recent update has been quite frustrating as I really like(d) this app.

First the good things. The app is pretty clean, low storage requirements, generally intuitive UI and overall aesthetic. You can listen to it on audio (I believe it requires an internet connection though). It has highlighting and commenting functions. It has the standard cross references. Bookmarks, text settings, etc etc, a decent app. 

However the app is also plagued by cons to just about any pro it has. In the version prior to this most recent update, the app would save your place (like most other Bible apps). It now resets to Genesis 1 every time you open the app. You could select the narrator before, and I enjoyed listening to Kristyn’s Irish accent. Now they’ve locked all but one voice behind a paywall. Also, you can only go up to 1.5x speed. As far as I can tell there’s no way to see all your comments or highlights on verses in one place. 

There’s more but those are my main gripes with how I use this app. I hate subscriptions and making accounts and this update seems to have pushed aggressively towards that. I’d be fine with a one-time payment for an account that I could transfer between devices, but I doubt that will happen. Even with all the negatives I still think this app is decent, but I will be keeping my eyes open for an alternative going forward.

Thank you. This is great! I used to use YouVersion, but it became so busy I don’t like it anymore. I have even started to shift back to my personal hard copy, and this app has probably helped. So good.

One request. Could you make some optional playback settings? I appreciate how in this app the Bible will just be read to me without chapter numbers interrupting the reading - that is how it was written to be read. However in the some books where chapters actually delineate distinct passages (psalms, most proverbs, and some prophets), breaks between chapters and reading of chapter numbers would be helpful. Can you make the reading of chapter numbers or at least pausing between chapters an optional playback setting?
